resources.convention: REST design. URLs name resources (plural nouns) with no verbs in the path; nest relations one level deep (`/issues/{id}/comments`). Use methods for what they mean: GET reads and never changes data, POST creates, PUT replaces the whole resource, PATCH changes part of it, DELETE removes. Status codes carry meaning: 200 read or update; 201 create, with a Location header; 204 delete; 400 bad input; 401 not authenticated; 403 not allowed; 404 not found; 409 conflict (for example a duplicate); use 422 only if the project's contract already does. Every error follows one project-wide shape (for example the Problem in the contract) with a message for a reader, never a stack trace or internal detail. An endpoint that returns a list must be bounded (pagination or a maximum size); filter and sort through query parameters. If the existing contract says otherwise than these general hints, follow the contract.

API backward compatibility: only add (new fields are optional and have defaults; new endpoints). Do not rename a field or change its meaning, do not change a type, do not narrow the accepted values, do not change an existing status code. A breaking change needs a new version and a transition period; a field that is going away is marked deprecated before it is removed. The contract comes before the code: change the spec first, then implement.
